vulnerability_patterns.description: Before the patch, `fscanf` used unbounded scanset specifiers to store whitespace/sign runs into caller-provided character arrays, allowing input longer than the destination buffers to overflow stack memory. The fix constrains each scanset write with an explicit field width, so the same sink becomes bounded.

The corresponding argument is a fixed-size character buffer such as `temp` or `signtmp`
Attacker-controlled file content contains a long run of characters accepted by the scanset, such as many spaces, tabs, or sign characters
The scanset conversion writes directly into the buffer before any later validation

Constrain each scanset sink at the parsing site instead of relying on later checks

shared_analysis.analysis_rationale: The only semantic change is in `src/bin/jp2/convert.c` at the `fscanf` call: several scanset conversions `%[ ... ]` were replaced with width-limited forms `%31[ ... ]`. In the old code, `fscanf` could write an unbounded number of matched characters into `temp` or `signtmp` before the `%d` fields were parsed, because scanset `%[` has no implicit bound. The patch adds explicit width barriers directly inside the format string, blocking overflow at the input sink itself rather than changing later logic.
